body: Some issues with the metadata fetcher
Metadata fetching looks good to me editorially now. Eager to hear others thoughts on whether it provides the right foundation for interoperability.

You also need to update the element indexes to include this attribute for img and iframe.

Should this influence https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-priority somehow?

Also: `img.decode()` waits for the image fetch to complete. With lazyload, this may take a long time, or might never happen. Is that the intent? Feels like `decode()` is a strong signal that the developer wants the image to fetch.

I’d suggest that since the change to the CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md files arenn’t directly related to the substance of the rest of this patch (lazyload feature), it’d be preferable for the CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md changes to be in separate patches from this patch. It’d be fine if they are just a separate commits as part of PR #3752 but not sure if that would happen, given that the policy here for PRs is that they result in a single (squashed) commit that gets merged to master
The changes to dev/style.css for adding the syntax-highlighter styles have already been merged into master, so they should be dropped from this patch.

OK, I’m now realizing that this reason some unrelated changes are showing up in the diff here are that this patch includes some merges? So it seems like it needs to be rebased against master to clear those away?

Some stuff to work out around images; I'm most concerned about srcset/picture.

Will look through other reviewers' comments and flag them also.
Small things and one big thing: what to do for srcset and picture.

So as I understand it from the text the scope here is reduced and the primary aim is to delay fetching initial(?) `img` or `iframe` resources until such a time they become visible to the user. I see some editorial issues and a number of processing model problems still.

Also, I need to hear from Apple on this as  @othermaciej and @smfr wrote a number of comments in #2806 that did not end up in the proposal. And while there was some back and forth it's not clear we have a full mutual understanding. (See also my question to @kinu above.)

Hope this helps.
Nice work @domfarolino, I like the new refactoring. I left 2 comments on things I think need further changes. The table you provided looks good. Agree about the word "hint".
Apologies, I haven't had the time to fully dig into this, but I thought I'd note some things from a quick read. I hope to have time for a more detailed review early next week.
Found a couple more points. Thanks for reducing the scope of this PR, that helps a lot!
I approved this because my comments were addressed. However, this still needs changes for the `load` event before merging, so marking as "request changes".
This looks pretty good, thanks! The interaction with Intersection Observer looks a little weird to me, but I'm not super knowledgeable about it either. Maybe @domenic has better suggestions for that.

I have a couple remaining nits, the biggest I'd be okay with as follow-up (doing state observation from something that runs in parallel). I think we already have implementation bugs and definitely have implementer interest, so the remaining things here are adequate test coverage, in particular for the various examples that came up during review and caught issues in Chrome.

Hope that helps and hope those taking a break soon have a good one!
Covering `<base>` explicitly is good as there are often issues around it, even if it theoretically feeds into a larger whole.
